title: Severe Storms Increase Electrical Risk and Mobilize Energisa
seoTitle: Severe Storms Raise Electrical Risk, Energisa Mobilizes
subtitle: Over 33,000 lightning strikes recorded in one week intensify alerts in western São Paulo state
excerpt: Between Saturday and Thursday, over 33,000 lightning strikes were recorded across 24 cities monitored by Energisa, leading the company to bolster 24/7 service.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Portal Prudentino, O Presente, Portal RSN
contentHtml:
Between last Saturday and Thursday, more than 33,000 lightning strikes were recorded across 24 cities monitored by power utility Energisa, raising the risk of power grid damage and prompting an increase in safety guidance.

Lightning and impacts on the power grid

Lightning strikes, accompanied by heavy rain and strong winds, increase the likelihood of fallen trees, downed power lines, and power supply interruptions. Energisa's Operations Manager, Alessandro Gomes Martins, emphasizes that continuous weather monitoring is essential to mobilize crews and coordinate with Civil Defense and firefighters.

Energisa's 24/7 customer service

In response to the rainy week, Energisa Sul-Sudeste is reinforcing its 24-hour customer service channels. Customers can reach the company via the Energisa On app, Gisa WhatsApp at (18) 99120-3365, Call Center at 0800 701 0326, or through the website energisa.com.br, including to report power outages or electrical hazards.

Safety measures for the public

During storms, residents should avoid handling metal objects connected to the electrical grid, such as refrigerators and stoves, and unplug electronic devices when safe to do so. It is also recommended to seek shelter in safe places, stay away from windows, trees, utility poles, and metal structures, and refrain from crossing flooded areas.

Emergency contact channels

In an emergency, in addition to Energisa's channels, Civil Defense can be reached via local phone numbers provided in the affected regions, and emergency services such as firefighters (193), police (190), and SAMU ambulance services (192) remain available.

Weather forecast and risks

In the Guarapuava region, meteorologists forecast heavy rain with accumulations that could exceed 100 mm throughout the week, wind gusts of up to 86 km/h, and possible hail. These conditions underscore the need to exercise extra caution around the electrical grid and follow guidance from authorities.

With information from Portal Prudentino, O Presente, and Portal RSN.
